title: Dedicated Capacity Navigator — Ops Workbench for compute-reserve health and scaling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Create a single-pane Ops Workbench — 'Dedicated Capacity Navigator' — that surfaces compute-reserve health, autoscaling controls, and burst tuning for Dedicated customers. The goal is to reduce MTTI for on-call engineers and provide product teams with an actionable view to control cost/latency trade-offs during traffic spikes.
summary: Design a compact, actionable dashboard and controls surface for Dedicated capacity (compute-reserve) focusing on health signals, autoscale tuning, and controlled burst windows. Includes prototype flows for canary rollouts tied to capacity allocations.
tasks: Finalize high-fidelity mockups for the 'Health Ribbon' and 'Burst Composer' widgets
Prototype interactive autoscale policy editor (min/max/scale-step + predicted latency curve)
Design fallback & rollback affordances for canary rollouts tied to compute-reserve labels
Document UX heuristics for cost visibility (per-reserve token-cost, burst-metering)
Handoff spec to ENG with component list and accessibility notes
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma prototype shows Health Ribbon, Burst Composer, Autoscale Editor, and Rollout controls
Prototype demonstrates a 3-step canary flow that can be mapped to existing rollout API (PM/ENG validation)
Design spec includes data dependencies and signal definitions (e.g., KV cache hit rate, request queue depth, burst credits remaining)
UX passes internal design review and an ops tabletop session (notes attached)
Handoff includes CSS tokens, responsive breakpoints, and an ARIA plan for interactive controls
decisions: Surface a compact single-line 'Health Ribbon' summarizing: node-heartbeats, GPU utilization percentile, KV cache hit rate, and error-rate — prioritized for scannability over raw metrics
Move detailed telemetry to a secondary 'Inspector' flyout to keep the main canvas focused on actions
Expose a bounded 'Burst Composer' that lets users schedule a burst window with a cost-estimate preview and an automatic decay policy
Autoscale editor will default to recommended profile (conservative) with a prominent 'Apply & Simulate' step to preview predicted latency/cost curves
Canary rollouts are linked to reserve-labels instead of per-instance selection to simplify mapping for Dedicated customers
comments: 2026-02-24 — Ava Martinez: Initial concept ready. Kept health canvas minimal to avoid cognitive overload. Attached three layout variants (left-rail, top-ribbon, and card-grid).

2026-03-01 — Priya Kapoor: PM feedback — include an explicit estimated cost delta when applying burst windows. Also ask ENG to return feasibility for live simulation data (latency forecast) within UI.

2026-03-04 — Marco Ruiz: Engineering notes — simulation requires a sampled prediction service; can mock for prototype. Also need agreements on signal names (we recommended 'kv_cache_hit_1m', 'gpu_util_p95').
2026-03-07 — Sophia Nguyen: Design review — prefer top-ribbon layout for quick scannability on wide consoles. Suggested micro-interactions for burst slider and a confirmable 'dry-run' mode.
2026-03-10 — Ethan Park: SRE review — ensure rollback action is a single-click with automatic drain and fallback to regional capacity. Add incident playbook links to the Inspector.
2026-03-11 — Liam Chen: Updated prototype linked; added 'Apply & Simulate' step and cost-preview. Need validation from Finance on cost calculation formula.
notes: Prototype intentionally avoids exposing low-level node identifiers; we map actions to reserve groups to keep dedicated tenant UX tractable. Finance asks to flag burst-initiated costs to billing as 'burst-surcharge' for auditing.
handoff_instructions: Include component props table, mock API responses for simulation, and a short video walkthrough (60s) showing the canary rollout + rollback flow. Engineers should be able to build static prototype from Figma tokens and mocked endpoints.
next_steps: ENG to prototype mock-sim service and return latency prediction SLA
Run ops tabletop with SRE and support to validate emergency rollback UX
Finalize accessibility review and add keyboard-only interactions
